name: Pointer events (mouse, pen, touch detail)
plain: Reports pointer position and, for pens and touch, pressure, tilt and contact size.
meaning: Mouse paths, speed and hesitation are strong behavioral signals (bot detection, attention tracking). Pen and touch fields add pressure and tilt that can tell devices apart.

web.api: pointerdown/move/up; PointerEvent.pressure, tiltX, tiltY, width, height, pointerType; getCoalescedEvents(); pointerrawupdate

access.persistence: While the pointer is over the page
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Events go to the frame under the pointer; no cross-origin leak across frames
steps: Person moves the pointer or touches
pointermove events fire (usually once per frame, or at the device rate with getCoalescedEvents)

limits.headline: Can see where your mouse, finger or pen is and how it moves on the page
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens while you move or tap over the page
can: Follow the path and speed of your mouse, finger or pen
Measure pen pressure, tilt and finger contact size where the device allows it
Tell humans from bots by how you move
Learn where you hesitate or hover
cannot: See where you point on other pages or in other apps
See movement when the page is in the background
Show a permission pop up; there is none
limits.reach_label: Every move while the page is open

story.what_it_is: The page sees where your mouse, pen or finger is, how fast it moves, and how hard you press.

marketing.name: Pointer events
marketing.pitch: Describes one set of events for mouse, pen and touch, with extras like pressure and tilt for pens.

story.for_you: You move, click, draw or swipe and the page responds smoothly. You may not notice it also sees the path your pointer takes and how long you pause. A pen can add pressure and tilt, so lines look natural.
story.for_makers: Mice and pens drive games and creative tools. Makers also study movement patterns to detect bots, find confusing parts of a page and tune ads and layouts.

use_cases.example: A browser game reads mouse position and clicks many times a second for aiming and dragging.
A web drawing tool uses pen pressure and tilt to vary line thickness.
A whiteboard app shows teammates' live cursors by sending pointer positions to others.
A heatmap tool records where visitors move and click to show the busy parts of a page.
A bot detector checks if the mouse path is a perfect straight line, a sign of a script.
An ad network measures hover time over an ad as a sign of attention.
A bank adds mouse habits to its risk score for a login.

technical_bounds: Sees pointer only inside its own viewport (and over its iframes' areas as the iframe's events)
pressure is 0 to 1 (0.5 for devices without pressure while a button is down); tiltX and tiltY are -90 to 90 degrees; twist 0 to 359
Coalesced events can expose input at 120 Hz or more (Chrome 58 and later, Firefox 59, Safari 18.2 per BCD)
pointerType is mouse, pen or touch; width and height reveal finger contact size (CSS px)
No pointer data while the pointer is outside the viewport, except with setPointerCapture or Pointer Lock

history.change: Pointer Events ship in Chrome stable
